# Executive Audit

## Purpose
Assess the state of the Executive department in the whole system: how well founder direction, investor relations, board reporting, and diligence readiness hold together, and where they are weak.

## Scope
- Founder context and priorities
- Investor relations and fundraising readiness
- Board updates and executive reporting
- Decision records
- Diligence material, kept ready to share

## What is in place
- [ ] Lead agent for the department is named and active
- [ ] Skill that keeps founder context current
- [ ] Skill that builds investor material and pitch decks
- [ ] Skill that researches investors and market context
- [ ] Command that produces a board update
- [ ] Workflow that keeps diligence material ready to share
- [ ] Decision log the founder can read back later

## Gaps
- [ ] Board and executive reporting is thin or ad hoc
- [ ] No chief-of-staff style support for founder execution
- [ ] Founder narrative is scattered across notes and chats
- [ ] Investor and market context is out of date
- [ ] Decision records are missing or hard to find
- [ ] Diligence material is not ready to share on short notice

## Next steps
- Pick the highest priority gap and name its owner
- Add or fix the missing agent, skill, command, or workflow for that gap
- Run the new piece on a real board update or investor task and check the result against evidence
- Record the decision and the outcome in the decision log
- Repeat for the next gap
- Share the finished audit and the changes with the people who need them, so the work reaches distribution
